title: Role model reconciliation and audit-forwarding playbook for RBAC v2 migration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket captures the operational playbook for migrating customers from the legacy RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 with a focus on two hard requirements: (1) identical effective permissions post-cutover, and (2) continuous, tamper-evident audit forwarding that preserves historical action context. Workstreams include a dual-write shadow mode, near-real-time reconciliation workers, audit-forwarding pipelines, SAML/SSO mapping verification, admin delegation migration, and a clearly defined cutover/rollback window. The playbook emphasizes conservative default behavior (deny-by-default fallback) and customer safety: no silent permission expansions, staged rollouts, and explicit customer opt-in for any aggressive backfills.
migration_steps: 1) Instrument dual-write in gateway: write to v1 authoritative store and v2 shadow store with identical request IDs for correlation.
2) Enable audit-forwarding bridge: stream v1 and v2 audit events to a secure audit-index with tags to identify origin and correlation IDs.
3) Run daily reconciliation sweepers (probabilistic + deterministic paths) to surface divergent role bindings and permission sets.
4) Surface high-risk divergences to a human-reviewed triage queue (SRE/Security/PM) for fixes or mitigation rules.
5) Execute a phased cutover: small canary customers -> internal test orgs -> 5% production -> 25% -> 100% with pause/rollback gates.
6) Post-cutover monitoring and one-week regression audit: confirm no unauthorized access with forensic sampling and synthetic scenario checks.
reconciliation_strategy: Continuous reconciler with three modes: shadow-only reporting, auto-suggest (propose changes to v1/v2), and cautious-apply (apply limited fixes with human approval).
Use deterministic hashing on principals + resource paths to bucket workloads and parallelize checks without blowing read quotas.
Sample smartly: 100% checks for admin-level bindings, 5% for low-risk service accounts; increase sample rate on any anomaly.
verification_checks: Permission parity check: effective permission matrix for 50 representative resources across roles must match within tolerance before enabling next rollout gate.
SAML mapping sanity: compare external_id -> principal mapping for top 10 IdPs in production and ensure no missing attribute mappings.
Audit continuity: for a set of correlated request IDs, events from v1 and v2 must appear in audit-index and maintain causal ordering.
Synthetic smoke tests: ACL exercises (create/read/update/delete) for canary orgs validated end-to-end including console and API paths.
rollback_plan: If parity divergence > threshold or customer-reported permission loss, flip routing back to v1 authoritative store and continue dual-write for observation.
Automated mitigation: deploy temporary deny-except rules to limit risky operations while investigation proceeds.
Post-rollback action: create hotfix runbook to reconcile data drift (export v2 deltas, apply to v1 or mute v2 until resolved).
audit_forwarding_notes: Audit bridge will inject 'rbac_migration_correlation_id' and 'origin_store' fields into events for end-to-end tracing.
All audit streams must be signed and retain immutability markers for at least 13 months per compliance requirements.
Forwarded events will be routed to the centralized audit-index and a read-only backup for forensic exports.
communications: Customer comms draft: staged notice with timeline, expected impact (read-only during backfill windows), and opt-out instructions for auto-backfill.
Internal runbook: Slack escalation playbook, on-call SRE and Security pager rotas, and response templates for customer support.
External status page entries and scheduled RFC docs (Confluence link stub to be added) for transparency during canary and mass cutover.
acceptance_criteria: No unexpected permission escalations observed in canary cohort for 72 hours after canary cutover.
Automated reconciler false positive rate < 0.5% for admin bindings across sampled orgs.
Audit-index contains correlated event pairs for 99.9% of sampled request IDs during dual-write window.
Security review sign-off completed and QA smoke tests green for console and API permission paths.
notes: Early tests revealed a mismatch in resource path normalization between v1 and v2; normalization shim implemented in gateway to fix canonicalization.
We should avoid global eager backfills; instead prioritize customer-safe heuristics and human-in-the-loop for admin roles.
Plan to coordinate with Platform Networking for maintenance windows that may affect SAML IdP reachability during cutover.
